about: Tuning values for the game and the level generator. Edit freely; every key is described in its section's _doc. Design references (D...) point to docs/DESIGN.md.

_doc.C: Track pieces made from one wood plus one ore (D6a.5, D9a.2).
_doc.bridgeTrees: Wood needed per bridge cell over water or lower ground (D4.8).
_doc.carryMax: Most items of one kind a player carries at once; upgrades may raise it (D6a.7).
_doc.storageMax: Most of each resource a storage wagon holds: this many wood and this many ore; upgrades may raise it (D6a.25).
_doc.trackMax: Most track pieces the crafting wagon holds; crafting waits while the next pair's pieces would not fit; upgrades may raise it (D6a.30).
_doc.hitsPerBlock: Hits to chop one forest block or mine one grey rock block (D6a.8).
_doc.hitSeconds: Time one hit takes, in seconds (D6a.8).
_doc.craftSecondsPerPair: Crafting wagon time per wood + ore pair, in seconds (D6a.5).
_doc.timerSlack: Level timer = time to cover max(T, R) * C cells at level speed, times this (D6a.3).
_doc.startTrack: Track pieces in a pile on the ground beside the front of the train when a level starts (D6.9).
_doc.dynamiteWood: Wood the dynamite wagon takes to make one stick; players put it in beside the wagon; upgrades may lower it (D6.12).
_doc.dynamiteOre: Ore the dynamite wagon takes to make one stick (D6.12).
_doc.dynamiteSeconds: Time the dynamite wagon takes to make one stick, in seconds (D6.12).
_doc.dynamiteMax: Most sticks the dynamite wagon holds (D6.12).
_doc.fuseSeconds: Seconds from lighting a stick to its blast, in hand, thrown or placed (D6.12).
_doc.blastRadius: Cells within this distance of a blast lose their trees and grey rock, and players there die (D6.12).
_doc.throwRange: Farthest throw on level ground, in cells, after holding the action for throwHoldSeconds (D6.12).
_doc.throwHoldSeconds: Holding the action this long gives the full throw; a short press puts the stick down instead (D6.12).

_doc.speed: Level speed in cells per second, held constant once reached (D6a.4). Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.acceleration: Speed gained per second when starting from a stop, in cells per second squared (D6a.4). Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.speedPerWagon: Level speed added for each wagon won at a station (each car beyond the starting three), in cells per second (D6.7). Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.startDelay: Countdown to the train setting off, in seconds, from the start pad being filled on a run's first level, and from the station's upgrade being picked or lost on later levels (D6.7, D6.9).
_doc.collideRadius: Radius of the circles that make up each car for collisions with characters, in cells (D6a.16).
_doc.crashSeconds: Wait after the train derails (or the level timer runs out) before the level restarts, in seconds.
_doc.fastForward: Fast-forward: the train's speed is multiplied by this while a player holds the fast-forward control, and once the line reaches the end station (D6a.28).

_doc.wedgeSeconds: A character pinned by the train against something it cannot move into dies only after this long, in seconds (D6a.16).
_doc.walkSpeed: Walking speed, in cells per second. Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.boostSpeed: Speed during a boost, in cells per second (D4.9). Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.boostSeconds: How long a boost lasts, in seconds. Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.boostCooldown: Least time between two boosts, in seconds (D3.7).
_doc.pushSpeed: Speed at which the train pushes a character aside, in cells per second (D6a.16). Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.respawnSeconds: Time from death to respawn near the train, in seconds (D6a.31). Placeholder, not tuned.
_doc.denySeconds: How long the red cross over a character shows a refused action (taking out a tool with nowhere to put what it carries), in seconds (D6a.20).

_doc.countdownSeconds: Time at a station before the next level starts (D6.7).
_doc.dwellSeconds: Time a player stands in an option's shadow, or on the start pad, to choose it (D6.7, D6.9).

_doc.windowCells: Width of the visible window of the level along x, in cells (D2.1). Everything outside it is clipped (D2.2).
_doc.cameraHeight: Camera height above the followed character, in cells.
_doc.cameraBack: Camera distance south of the followed character, in cells.
_doc.waterLevel: Height of a water surface within its top block, as a fraction of the block (1 = level with the ground around it).
_doc.itemSize: Side of a wood or ore cube, in cells, in hands, in stacks and on the wagon.
_doc.trainScale: Size of the locomotive and wagons, 1 = the models' own; 1.1 puts them just under the 2 cells each takes on the track (D6a.26).
_doc.waterVariety: Water: a slow swell whose strength wanders over the level, a slightly different shade per cell, and now and then a faint ring spreading in a cell (D11.17).
_doc.toolScale: Size of the pickaxe and axe in a character's hand; 1 = about a quarter of the character's height, 2 = about half (D11a.5).
_doc.arCellSize: AR mode: size of one cell in metres when the board is first put on the table; hands resize it after (D3.5).
_doc.arWindowCells: AR mode: width of the visible window of the level along x, in cells (the desktop uses windowCells).
_doc.arStickPanCells: AR mode: while one controller grip is held, the right thumbstick slides the view along the level this many cells a second at full tilt.
_doc.palette: Experiment (D11.19): each level takes one of 500 colour palettes for its ground, trees, water and rock, mixing into the next level's around the station between them. Off: the usual colours.
_doc.paletteSeed: Which palettes the levels get; change it to try others (any whole number).
_doc.paletteStrength: How far the colours move toward the palette: 0 = the usual colours, 1 = the palette's.
_doc.paletteBlendCells: Width in cells of the band around the station between two levels where their palettes mix cell by cell.
_doc.weather: Rain and snow (D11.20): each level is clear, rainy or snowy, the same for everyone in the room. Off: always clear.
_doc.rainChance: Chance a level is rainy, 0 to 1.
_doc.snowChance: Chance a level is snowy, 0 to 1 (rainChance + snowChance at most 1; the rest is clear).
_doc.weatherBlendCells: Width in cells of the band around the station between two levels where their weathers mix.
_doc.rainDrops: Raindrops falling over the visible window at once (up to 3000).
_doc.snowFlakes: Snowflakes falling over the visible window at once (up to 2000).
_doc.rainSplash: Share of raindrops that leave a small ring where they land, 0 to 1.
_doc.rainVoxels: Size of a raindrop's cubes on the page, in terrain voxels (a 32nd of a cell); cubes sit on the grid of their size.
_doc.arRainVoxels: Size of a raindrop's cubes in AR, in terrain voxels.
_doc.rainStreak: Cubes in one raindrop, 1 to 4, a slanted staircase.
_doc.rainSlant: How far rain falls sideways: voxels across per voxel down (0 = straight down).
_doc.rainSpeed: How fast rain falls, in cells a second.
_doc.puddles: Share of plain ground cells in rainy levels with a puddle, 0 to 1.
_doc.birds: Bird flocks crossing, circling and landing over the board (D11.21); they fly off when something happens near them.
_doc.birdFlocks: How many flocks come and go over the board.
_doc.swingsPerSecond: How fast characters swing the pickaxe and axe, in swings per second (the model's own speed is 2.4). Each pickaxe swing plays a mine sound as it strikes. How fast blocks break is rules.hitSeconds (2 = one swing per hit).
_doc.soundVolume: Loudness of all sound effects, 0 to 1.
_doc.soundHalfCells: Distance in cells from this player's character at which a sound is half as loud; farther is softer still.
_doc.hornWarnCells: The horn starts warning when the train has this many cells of track left before the end, sounding more often as it gets closer.
_doc.bloom: Bloom filter: bright parts of the picture glow.
_doc.bloomStrength: How strong the glow is (0 = none).
_doc.bloomRadius: How far the glow spreads, 0 to 1.
_doc.bloomThreshold: Brightness above which a pixel glows (scene brightness; the lit tops of pale blocks reach about 1).
_doc.ao: Corner shading: tops darken where higher columns stand beside them (D11.11).
_doc.aoStrength: How dark fully shaded corners get, 0 to 1.
_doc.groundDetail: Ground tops with mottled dirt, loam blotches, pebble clusters and cracks (D11.11).
_doc.groundPatches: Broad light/dark and warm/cool colour patches across the ground, greener near forests (D11.11).
_doc.groundPatchStrength: How strong the ground colour patches are (0 = none).
_doc.groundPatchScale: Size of the ground colour patches, in cells.
_doc.groundDecor: Ground details: fallen leaves near forests, gravel near grey rock, pebbles, flower patches (D11.11).
_doc.groundDecorDensity: How many ground details (1 = default amount, 0 = none).
_doc.groundTints: Each ground cell gets one of a set of mild colour tints, at random (D11.15).
_doc.groundTintCount: How many of the 16 tints are used (1 to 16).
_doc.groundTintStrength: How strong the tints are (1 = default, 0 = none, 2 = double).
_doc.treeTints: Each tree gets one of a set of mild green tints, at random (D11.15).
_doc.treeTintCount: How many of the 16 tree tints are used (1 to 16).
_doc.treeTintStrength: How strong the tree tints are (1 = default, 0 = none, 2 = double).
_doc.blackTints: Each black rock column gets one of a set of mild grey tints, at random (D11.15).
_doc.blackTintCount: How many of the 16 black rock tints are used (1 to 16).
_doc.blackTintStrength: How strong the black rock tints are (1 = default, 0 = none, 2 = double).
_doc.rockTints: Each grey rock cell gets one of a set of mild grey tints, at random (D11.15).
_doc.rockTintCount: How many of the 16 grey rock tints are used (1 to 16).
_doc.rockTintStrength: How strong the grey rock tints are (1 = default, 0 = none, 2 = double).
_doc.rockPatterns: With brickRelief: how many of the 8 stone patterns grey rock uses (1 to 8) (D11.14).
_doc.rockPatternScale: With brickRelief: grey rock keeps one pattern over regions about this many cells across; 0 picks per cell at random.
_doc.treeVariety: Forests with trees of varied size, turn and colour, some spots empty or holding a bush (D11.11).
_doc.treeFill: Share of the nine tree spots per forest cell that hold a tree (at least two).
_doc.treeScaleJitter: Tree sizes vary by up to this fraction either way.
_doc.treeTint: How much tree colours vary (0 = all the same).
_doc.treeSway: Trees and bushes sway in the wind (their shadows do not).
_doc.rockBoulders: Grey rock drawn as piles of boulders instead of a block (D11.11).
_doc.boulderSpill: How far boulders reach past their cell's edge, in cells.
_doc.crags: Jagged spires on black rock tops, taller inside mountains (D11.11).
_doc.cragDensity: Chance per black rock cell of crags (0 to 1).
_doc.blackStrata: Black rock sides banded in layers (D11.11).
_doc.designedTiles: Pixel-art tile faces drawn to a plan: small palettes, lit rims along ledges, a few variants and rare specials (D11.12). Off: the voxel models' own faces.
_doc.carvedBlack: With designedTiles: black rock carved like old ruins, from etqws3's CC0 blocks recoloured (D11.13).
_doc.carvedRelief: With carvedBlack: the carving is raised as a voxel heightfield by class (blocks from tools/carvevox.ts).
_doc.brickRock: With designedTiles: grey rock is stone blocks from SpiderDave's CC0 Techno Bricks, recoloured; mining adds cracks (D11.14).
_doc.brickRelief: With brickRock: joints and cracks sunk, stones raised, as a voxel heightfield (blocks from tools/brickvox.ts).
_doc.edgeLines: A dark line along every exposed top edge.
_doc.faceDecor: Small pieces on exposed block sides: vines on black rock walls, grass hanging over forest ledges, stones in dirt sides (D11.12).
_doc.faceDecorDensity: How many face pieces (1 = default amount, 0 = none).
_doc.showColliders: Draw what the game collides with: each character's circle (as a cylinder), the train's circles, the start pad's circle, and the cells blocking your character (red squares).

_doc.keyboard: Keys per action, as browser physical key codes (KeyW, ArrowUp, Space, ...). Several keys may share an action. Per-person changes go in config/keys/<name>.json, loaded with ?keys=<name> (D3.8).
_doc.gamepad: Standard-mapping gamepad: which stick moves and which picks emotes, and button numbers, one or a list (0 A, 1 B, 2 X, 3 Y, 6 left trigger, 7 right trigger, 8 back/view, 9 start/menu, 11 right stick press, 14/15 d-pad left/right). fastForward (held) speeds the train up (D6a.28); 4 is the left bumper. Keyboard and gamepad only: cameraMode steps the camera through following the train, following your character, and free; cameraSnap drops a camera pan (free camera: jumps to your character); toolPrev/toolNext step through pickaxe, axe, no tool, and a button shared with emoteSend sends while the emote menu is open and steps the tool otherwise (keyboard also pickaxe, axe, noTool to choose one); help shows the key list.
_doc.xr: AR controllers (WebXR): hand and control name per action. Controls: thumbstick, thumbstick-press, trigger, x, y (left hand), a, b (right hand). The squeeze (grip) grabs the board (D3.9). toolPrev/toolNext step through pickaxe, axe, no tool; a control shared with emoteSend sends while the emote menu is open and steps the tool otherwise. cameraMode picks what the board keeps in its middle (the train, your character, or nothing); cameraSnap drops a drag of the level.
_doc.deadzone: Stick values below this are ignored (0 to 1).
_doc.throwPitch: In AR, while aiming a lit stick (action held), the tilt of the action button's controller sets how far it goes: pointing at or below the first angle throws one cell, at or above the second the full rules.throwRange, in between in proportion. Degrees above level (negative is pointing down). Keyboard and gamepad keep the hold-to-charge throw.

_doc.tickHz: Simulation ticks per second on the server (D7.2).

_doc.length: Cells from start to end, along x.
_doc.chokes: Number of black rock walls across the level; each has a narrow gap (route A) and a wide gap (route B) (D9a).
_doc.narrowGap: Gap width range [min, max] for the narrow route A, in cells.
_doc.wideGap: Gap width range [min, max] for the wide route B, in cells.
_doc.chokeSeparation: Hint for the rows of black rock between the narrow and the wide gap in each choke wall: 0 for no preference, -1 for as far apart as the width allows. Best effort: the nearest separation that fits is used, never fewer than 2.
_doc.wallThickness: Choke wall thickness range [min, max] along x, in cells; each row's edges also move by up to a cell at random.
_doc.forestSize: Forest patch size range [min, max], in cells.
_doc.rockSize: Grey rock patch size range [min, max], in cells.
_doc.blackrockSize: Black rock patch size range [min, max], in cells.
_doc.pondSize: Pond size range [min, max], in cells.
_doc.levels: Number of ground height levels (1 = flat).
_doc.hillScale: Feature size of the height noise, in cells; larger = broader hills.
_doc.hillNoise: Amount of finer noise mixed into the height.
_doc.minBlob: Smallest area of one height, in cells; smaller areas merge into neighbours.
_doc.mountainStep: Black rock rises this many levels per step inward (D4.10).
_doc.mountainMax: Highest black rock rise, in levels.
_doc.rampChance: Chance per eligible cell on a level boundary of a pre-built grey rock ramp (0 = none).
_doc.pathRamps: Pre-build the ramps the cheapest track route needs (except ramps that would stand on a bridge).
_doc.sparseRadius: Forest and grey rock are not grown within this distance of route A (unless also near route B), so route A is light on resources. In cells.
_doc.minRatio: Accept a level only if every route's resource ratio (track the resources make / track needed) is at least this.
_doc.maxAttempts: Attempts before the generator gives up.
_doc.startY: Fixed start station row, or null to choose.
_doc.endY: Fixed end station row, or null to choose.
_doc.stationLength: Station length in cells along x. At least the train's length: 3 cars of 2 cells each.
